headline: A farmer's strange stone leads to giant statues

sources.title: An Egyptian Villager Stumbled Upon an Inscribed Stone. It Led to a Colossal Head of Ramses II (Gizmodo)
A Farmer in Egypt Stumbled Upon a Pink Stone and Called the Authorities. They Found the Remains of Two Colossal Statues of Ramses II Beneath the Property (Smithsonian Magazine)
Egypt discovers fragments of two colossal Ramses II statues (Gulf News)

chunks.text: A farmer in Egypt's Nile Delta was working on his land when he found a strange stone outside his home. It was covered in [[ancient writing]]. He reported it to local officials, and they {{brought in}} a team of [[archaeologists]]. In mid-October 2026, Egypt's Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities announced what the team had found. Under the farmer's land were parts of two [[giant statues]] of the [[pharaoh]] Ramses II.

verbs.correct: To ask experts to come and help
verbs.wrong: To close the area to visitors
verbs.why: The city brings in engineers to check old bridges. Hospitals bring in extra doctors in flu season. Local officials brought in a team of archaeologists.

chunks.text: The team {{dug up}} a stone head that is more than 5 feet tall. It shows Ramses II wearing a [[double crown]]. This crown was a sign of his [[rule]] over both Upper and Lower Egypt. Next to the head was part of the statue's back, carved with one of the king's names. From the size of the head, officials {{worked out}} that the [[complete]] statue was about 28 feet tall, including its [[base]].

verbs.correct: To remove something from the ground
verbs.wrong: To build a wall around a site
verbs.why: Dogs dig up bones in the backyard. Farmers dig up potatoes in the fall. The team dug up a stone head that is more than 5 feet tall.

verbs.correct: To find an answer by thinking or calculating
verbs.wrong: To clean a statue with soft brushes
verbs.why: I work out the tip in my head. Students work out the answer with a calculator. From the size of the head, officials worked out that the whole statue was about 28 feet tall.

chunks.text: A second statue {{turned up}} close by. It is nearly 8 feet tall, but its legs and base are [[missing]]. It wears a [[striped]] royal [[headcloth]], and experts believe it also shows Ramses II. Its face has {{held up}} well, with clear [[features]] like those of the first statue. The team also found a [[pink granite]] block more than 4 feet long. It carries two of the king's [[royal titles]]. The statues {{go back}} more than 3,200 years.

verbs.correct: To be found, often by chance
verbs.why: Lost keys often turn up in a coat pocket. My missing socks always turn up in the wash. A second statue turned up close by.

verbs.correct: To still be in good condition
verbs.why: Good leather shoes hold up for years. This old bridge still holds up in big storms. The face of the second statue has held up well.

verbs.correct: To have existed since a past time
verbs.wrong: To be worth a lot of money
verbs.why: This bakery goes back to 1920. My family's farm goes back four generations. The statues go back more than 3,200 years.

chunks.text: The village is best known for the [[ruins]] of a temple to a [[goddess]]. But experts {{point out}} that it was built many [[centuries]] after Ramses II. Experts now want to {{find out}} how the statues {{ended up}} there. The digging will {{carry on}} as researchers try to {{piece together}} the site's history. The farmer told reporters that he was surprised and happy. He said officials told him the find might change the history of the area.

verbs.correct: To tell people about a fact
verbs.wrong: To dig around a very old wall
verbs.why: Doctors point out that sleep is important for health. My teacher points out the mistakes in my writing. Experts point out that the temple was built many centuries after Ramses II.

verbs.correct: To learn a fact you did not know
verbs.wrong: To clean a stone very gently
verbs.why: Students find out their grades online. I usually find out the news from my phone. Experts now want to find out how the statues got to the village.

verbs.wrong: To be carved by a skilled worker
verbs.why: Lost balls often end up in the river. Many travelers end up in towns they never planned to visit. Nobody knows yet how the statues ended up in the village.
The game carries on after the rain stops. Work on the road carries on all summer. The digging at the site will carry on.

verbs.correct: To understand something from small facts
verbs.wrong: To write a short report about a king
verbs.why: Doctors piece together the cause of an illness from many tests. Detectives piece together a crime from small clues. Researchers will try to piece together the history of the site.

vocab.def: To ask experts to come and help

Our company brought in a lawyer to check the contract.

vocab.def: To remove something from the ground
ex: We dug up the old tree and planted a new one.
The kids dug up some coins in the park.
Workers dug up an old pipe under the street.

vocab.def: To find an answer by thinking or calculating
ex: Can you work out how much we each owe?
She worked out the distance on a map.
Engineers worked out the weight of the bridge before building it.

vocab.def: To be found, often by chance

vocab.def: To still be in good condition

vocab.def: To tell people about a fact

vocab.def: To understand something from small facts
ex: The police pieced together what happened from the camera videos.

wordDefs.def: Words or signs that people wrote thousands of years ago
ex: The museum shows ancient writing on clay tablets.
Few people today can read this ancient writing.
The cave walls are full of ancient writing and pictures.

wordDefs.def: Experts who study objects and places from the distant past
ex: Archaeologists found old tools near the river.
My cousin wants to work with archaeologists in Mexico.
The archaeologists spent the summer at the old fort.

wordDefs.def: Very large figures made of stone or metal
ex: Giant statues stand at the entrance to the park.
The island is famous for its giant statues.
Workers used cranes to move the giant statues.
The pharaoh lived in a large palace.
Each pharaoh wanted a great tomb.
The movie tells the story of a young pharaoh.

wordDefs.def: A two-part crown worn by the kings of ancient Egypt
ex: The painting shows a king in a double crown.
The double crown was red and white.
Only the king could wear the double crown.

wordDefs.def: The power to control a country
ex: The country grew rich under the queen's rule.
His rule lasted for thirty years.
Many people were unhappy with the king's rule.
I finally have a complete set of the books.
The puzzle is not complete; one piece is gone.
We found a complete skeleton of a small dinosaur.

wordDefs.def: The bottom part that something stands on
ex: The lamp has a heavy metal base.
There is a crack in the base of the vase.
The statue's base has the artist's name on it.

wordDefs.def: Not there, because it is lost or gone
ex: Two pages of this book are missing.
The police are looking for a missing dog.
One of my front buttons is missing.

wordDefs.def: Having long, thin lines of different colors
ex: He wore a blue and white striped shirt.
The cat has a striped tail.
We bought a striped umbrella for the beach.

wordDefs.def: A piece of cloth worn over the head
ex: The old woman wore a cotton headcloth in the sun.
In the photo, the farmer has a white headcloth.

wordDefs.def: The parts of a face, like the eyes, nose and mouth
ex: The baby has her father's features.
The artist drew his features very carefully.
Her features are soft and friendly.

wordDefs.def: A very hard, pink stone used for buildings and statues
ex: The new bank has steps made of pink granite.
Pink granite is common in this part of the state.
The kitchen counter is a slab of pink granite.

wordDefs.def: Official names that show someone is a king or queen
ex: The prince has several royal titles.
Her royal titles are printed on the letter.
He lost his royal titles when he left the family.

wordDefs.def: What is left of an old building after it is badly damaged
ex: We visited the ruins of an old castle.
Tourists take photos of the ruins every day.
The ruins are all that is left of the old city.
The Greeks had a goddess of love.
The temple has a statue of a goddess.
In the story, a goddess helps the hero.
The castle stood empty for centuries.
This recipe has been in our family for centuries.
People have farmed this valley for centuries.

mainIdea.s: A farmer reported an odd stone on his land in Egypt, and experts found two huge statues of Ramses II under it. They still want to learn how the statues came to be in his village.
mainIdea.why: The farmer found a stone, and officials brought in archaeologists. Experts now want to find out how the statues ended up there.

mainIdea.s: An Egyptian farmer found two enormous pharaoh statues in his field and dug them up by himself. Experts say the stones were made for the famous temple in his village, which is just as old.
mainIdea.why: Close, but a team of archaeologists dug up the statues. The temple was built many centuries after Ramses II, so nobody knows yet how they got there.

mainIdea.s: Egypt has opened a large new museum near Cairo to show objects from its ancient kings. Visitors can now see a famous statue of Ramses II that was moved there from a busy city square.
mainIdea.why: This story is about two statues that turned up under a farmer's land after he found a strange stone.

tf.s: A farmer found a strange stone while working on his land.
tf.why: It was covered in ancient writing. He reported it, and officials brought in a team of archaeologists.

tf.s: The statues turned up during work on a new road.
tf.why: They turned up under a farmer's land after he reported a strange stone to officials.

tf.s: Officials brought in archaeologists after the farmer reported the stone.
tf.why: Local officials asked a team of archaeologists to come, and the team found parts of two giant statues.

tf.s: Experts already know how the statues ended up in the village.
tf.why: Experts still want to find out how they got there, because the village temple was built centuries after Ramses II.

tf.s: The team has stopped digging at the site.
tf.why: The digging will carry on as researchers try to understand the history of the site.

tf.s: Experts believe both statues show the pharaoh Ramses II.
tf.why: The first head clearly shows him, and experts believe the second statue, which turned up close by, shows him too.

lines.text: Did you hear about the farmer in Egypt and the giant statues?
He was working on his land, and he found a strange stone with ancient writing on it.
He reported it, and officials {{brought in}} a team of archaeologists.
Good for him. He [[did the right thing]].
The team {{dug up}} a huge stone head of Ramses II. It's more than five feet tall.
So the whole statue must have been enormous.
Officials {{worked out}} it was about 28 feet. Then a second statue {{turned up}} close by.
Totally. And its face has {{held up}} really well.
A find like that happens [[once in a lifetime]].
The strange part is that nobody knows how they {{ended up}} in that village.
It [[makes you wonder]] what else is under those fields.
The team will {{carry on}} digging to {{find out}}.
I hope they can {{piece together}} the whole story.

expressions.def: Used to say that something is very surprising and unlikely
ex: We sat next to my old teacher on the plane. What are the odds?

expressions.def: Used to say that someone made a good and honest choice
ex: She gave the lost wallet to the police. She did the right thing.
I told my boss about the mistake, and I know I did the right thing.

expressions.def: Used to say that someone got something very good or valuable
ex: We hit the jackpot when we found this cheap apartment.

expressions.def: Used to say that something is very rare and may never happen again
ex: A trip like this happens once in a lifetime.
My grandparents say their trip to Japan was a chance that comes once in a lifetime.

expressions.def: Used to say that something makes you curious or a little doubtful
ex: The store is always empty. It makes you wonder how it stays open.
